note: The uSWID fuzzer input bytes are parsed as the FuStructUswid header, making the header fields attacker controlled.
The attacker-controlled header size selects where the coSWID CBOR payload begins in the same input stream.

code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
note: The attacker-controlled payload size and header size are used to extract the CBOR payload bytes that will be parsed as a coSWID image.
The extracted payload bytes are decoded by libcbor into map items whose integer storage width is determined by the CBOR encoding.
A version-scheme tag in the attacker-controlled CBOR map routes its value item to the version-scheme reader.
The code checks only that the CBOR value is an unsigned integer, but does not require that the item is encoded with at least uint16 storage before reading it as uint16.
For the candidate, the version-scheme value is encoded as a one-byte CBOR uint8, so cbor_get_uint16 reads two bytes from a smaller libcbor integer allocation.
